title: Atomics
narrative:
## Lock-Free Synchronization with Atomics

Atomic types (`AtomicInt`, `AtomicBool`) provide lock-free, thread-safe operations on primitive values. They're the fastest way to share data between threads.

### AtomicInt

```xiom
let counter = AtomicInt.new(0);

counter.add(1);              // atomic increment
let val = counter.load();    // atomic read — val = 1
counter.store(42);           // atomic write
```

### Common Atomic Operations

```xiom
let a = AtomicInt.new(0);

// Basic operations
a.store(10);                  // set value
a.add(5);                     // add (returns new value)
a.sub(1);                     // subtract
let v = a.load();             // get value

// Compare-And-Swap (CAS)
let old = a.compare_exchange(15, 20);
// if a == 15, set to 20; returns old value
```

### AtomicBool

```xiom
let flag = AtomicBool.new(false);
flag.store(true);              // set flag
let is_set = flag.load();      // read flag

// Compare and swap
let swapped = flag.compare_exchange(false, true);
// Atomically: if flag == false, set to true, return true
// if flag != false, return false
```

### Atomics vs Mutex

| Feature | Atomics | Mutex |
|---------|---------|-------|
| Types | Primitive only | Any type |
| Operations | Single operations | Complex logic |
| Blocking | Never (lock-free) | Yes |
| Speed | Fastest | Slower |
| Complexity | Harder to use correctly | Easier |

### Use Cases

- Simple counters
- Flags and state machines
- Lock-free data structures
- Performance-critical paths
tips: Atomics are lock-free — no blocking, fastest thread-safe operations
Use for simple counters and flags — not complex data structures
Compare-And-Swap (CAS) is the building block for lock-free algorithms
For complex shared state, use Mutex or RwLock instead
